body:
## Pull request overview

This PR standardizes “refresh after mutation” behavior across ObjectUI’s data-bound views by introducing a schema-level refresh signal, an imperative refresh API, and a DataSource mutation event bus that views can subscribe to for automatic re-fetching.

**Changes:**
- Added `refreshTrigger?: number` to `ListViewSchema` and wired it into ListView’s data-fetch effect dependencies.
- Introduced `DataSource.onMutation()` + `MutationEvent` and implemented emission/subscription (ValueDataSource + ListView/ObjectView/Kanban/Calendar auto-refresh).
- Added `ListView` imperative `ref.refresh()` plus a reusable `useDataRefresh()` hook and associated tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 17 out of 17 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListRefresh.test.tsx | Adds coverage for refreshTrigger, imperative refresh(), and `onMutation` auto-refresh. |
| packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx | Propagates refreshKey into rendered ListView + adds ObjectView `onMutation` subscription. |
| packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx | Adds standalone-mode `onMutation` refresh support for Kanban. |
| packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx | Adds standalone-mode `onMutation` refresh support for Calendar. |

`DataSource<T>` declares `onMutation` as `(event: MutationEvent) => void`, which drops the generic `T` and makes `event.record` effectively `any` even for typed data sources. Consider changing this to `onMutation?(callback: (event: MutationEvent<T>) => void): () => void` so typed adapters (like `ValueDataSource<T>`) preserve record typing end-to-end.
```suggestion
  onMutation?(callback: (event: MutationEvent<T>) => void): () => void;
```
